title: Elimination of indeterminacy on a regular Noetherian surface
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Let $X\to S$ be an integral regular Noetherian scheme of dimension $2$ [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-regular-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], where Noetherian means locally Noetherian and quasi-compact. Let $Y\to S$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], let $U\subseteq X$ be a dense open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion], and let $f:U\to Y$ be an $S$-morphism. There exist $n\geq0$, a tower $X_n\xrightarrow{b_n}\cdots\xrightarrow{b_1}X_0=X$ of blowups of reduced closed points [def-nagata-global-blowup], and an $S$-morphism $g:X_n\to Y$. Every centre lies outside the inverse image of $U$. Every $X_i$ is integral, regular, Noetherian and of dimension $2$. The composite $p:X_n\to X$ is proper and is an isomorphism over $U$, and $g|_{p^{-1}(U)}=f\circ p|_{p^{-1}(U)}$. Length zero is allowed.

source.place: Tag 0C5H (resolve-lemma-extend-rational-map-blowing-up), with regular surface preservation from Tag 0AGR (resolve-lemma-blowup-regular). The point-blowup tower in 0C5H is through regular surfaces; the properness and Noetherianity conclusions are the usual finite-type blowup properties.

proof.text: Consider all pairs $(V,F)$ with $U\subseteq V\subseteq X$ open and $F:V\to Y$ an $S$-morphism extending $f$. This family is nonempty since it contains $(U,f)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal] to their closed complements to choose $(V,F)$ for which $T=X\setminus V$ is minimal under inclusion. Thus $F$ cannot be extended to any strictly larger open containing $V$.

source.place: Tag 0C5H, proof, first sentence; Noetherian maximal-domain implementation of the enlargement of U.

proof.text: By [lem-sc-scheme-stalk-dimension-generalization-chains] and $\dim X=2$, every local ring has dimension at most $2$. An integral scheme has a unique generic point $\eta$, by [def-pc-integral-scheme] and [lem-sc-scheme-sober]; it belongs to every nonempty open, hence to $U$. Every other point has $\eta$ as a strict generalization, so has local dimension at least $1$. If $x\notin V$ had local dimension $1$, its local ring would be regular by [def-weil-regular-scheme] and a DVR by [lem-sc-regular-dim1-dvr], hence a valuation ring by [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring]. Apply [lem-sfb-rational-map-extension-valuation-point] with dense open $V$ and map $F$ to extend across $x$, contradicting step 1. Consequently $\dim\mathcal O_{X,t}=2$ for every $t\in T$.

source.place: Tag 0C5H, proof, first sentence; the DVR criterion is algebra.tex Tag 00PD (lemma-characterize-dvr), (3) implies (2).

proof.text: Every $t\in T$ is closed in $X$: otherwise a strict specialization of $t$ could be prefixed to a length-two generalization chain starting at $t$, contradicting $\dim X=2$. Here the existence of that chain follows from [lem-sc-scheme-stalk-dimension-generalization-chains], since a supremum of integer chain lengths equal to $2$ is attained. The closed set $T$ is finite. Indeed, if it were not a finite union of singleton closed subsets, choose a minimal closed subset $C\subseteq T$ failing this property, by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal]. It is neither empty nor a singleton. It cannot be irreducible, since its generic point given by [lem-sc-scheme-sober] is a point of $T$, hence closed in $X$. Thus $C=C_1\cup C_2$ for two proper closed subsets; their minimality gives finite singleton decompositions, a contradiction. The empty $T$ is permitted.

source.place: Tag 0C5H, proof, second sentence: the complement is a finite set of regular dimension-two closed points; chain and Noetherian arguments expanded.

proof.text: The inclusion $j:V\hookrightarrow X$ is quasi-compact. To see this directly from [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal], ascending chains of open subsets of $X$ terminate, so among finite subunions of any family of opens there is a maximal one; it contains every member of that family and equals its union. Thus every open subspace of $X$ is quasi-compact. In particular the intersection of $V$ with any affine open of $X$ is quasi-compact, which is exactly the required quasi-compactness of the open immersion $j$.

source.place: Tag 0C4V (divisors-lemma-extend-rational-map-after-modification), proof: the domain open is retrocompact because X is Noetherian.

proof.text: Let $a=(j,F):V\to X\times_S Y$ and let $i:Z=\operatorname{SIm}(a)\hookrightarrow X\times_S Y$ be its scheme-theoretic image, with factor map $a^{\mathrm{im}}$, as in [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image]. Write $q=\operatorname{pr}_X i$ and $F_Z=\operatorname{pr}_Y i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-proper-base-change], $\operatorname{pr}_X$ is proper; [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper](b) makes $q$ proper. Properness includes separatedness by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Hence [lemma-nagata-scheme-image-partial-section], using the quasi-compact inclusion from step 4 and separated $Y\to S$, says that $q^{-1}(V)\to V$ is an isomorphism. The equality $i a^{\mathrm{im}}=a$ gives $q a^{\mathrm{im}}=j$ and $F_Z a^{\mathrm{im}}=F$. Therefore $F_Z|_{q^{-1}(V)}=F\circ q|_{q^{-1}(V)}$. Both projections are over $S$, so $F_Z$ is an $S$-morphism when $Z$ is given its structure through $q$.

source.place: Tag 0C4V (divisors-lemma-extend-rational-map-after-modification), proof in full: scheme-theoretic graph image; used by Tag 0C5H after enlarging U.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-regular-point-blowup-domination] to $q:Z\to X$ and the finite set $T$. Its hypotheses hold: $X$ is Noetherian; every point of $T$ is closed with regular local ring of dimension $2$ by steps 2--3; and $q$ is proper and an isomorphism over $V=X\setminus T$ by step 5. Obtain a finite tower $X_n\xrightarrow{b_n}\cdots\xrightarrow{b_1}X_0=X$ and $h:X_n\to Z$ with $qh=p=b_1\cdots b_n$. Each centre is a reduced closed point mapping to $T$, hence lies outside the inverse image of the original $U\subseteq V$. Equip every $X_i$ with the $S$-structure obtained by composing with $X\to S$.

source.place: Tag 0C5H, proof, last two sentences, invoking Tag 0AHI (resolve-lemma-dominate-by-blowing-up-in-points).

proof.text: Induct on $i$ with invariant: $X_i$ is integral, regular and Noetherian; each earlier blowup is proper and an isomorphism away from its centre; and every closed point of $X_i$ mapping into $T$ has local dimension $2$. The base follows from the hypotheses and steps 2--3. The next centre is such a closed point. Apply [lem-sfb-regular-point-blowup-geometry] at that centre: it gives the first two parts of the invariant on $X_{i+1}$. To check the last part, let $r\in X_{i+1}$ be closed over $T$. Since $b_{i+1}$ is proper, hence closed by [def-weil-proper-morphism], its image is a closed point of $X_i$. If this image is the centre, the same geometry node gives $\dim\mathcal O_{X_{i+1},r}=2$; otherwise the isomorphism away from the centre identifies this local ring with the dimension-two local ring supplied by the induction hypothesis. This proves the invariant, including when $T$ is empty (the tower then has no centres).

source.place: Tag 0AGR (resolve-lemma-blowup-regular) through the existing global point-blowup geometry node; preservation along the tower of Tag 0C5H.

proof.text: For use in the dimension check, every point $z$ of a Noetherian scheme $W$ has a closed specialization. Choose a minimal nonempty closed subset $C\subseteq\overline{\{z\}}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal]. For every $c\in C$, minimality gives $\overline{\{c\}}=C$. Uniqueness of generic points in [lem-sc-scheme-sober] implies that all these $c$ coincide, so $C$ is a singleton closed in $W$. Moreover, [lem-sc-scheme-stalk-dimension-generalization-chains] shows that the local dimension at $z$ is at most the local dimension at a specialization of $z$. Finally, by the same chain formula and [lem-sc-scheme-sober], $\dim W$ is the supremum of its local-ring dimensions: a chain of irreducible closed subsets becomes the chain of their generic points and conversely. These arguments apply without separatedness or a Jacobson hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 02IZ (properties-lemma-codimension-local-ring) and schemes.tex Tag 01IS (lemma-scheme-sober); elementary consequences needed for the extra dimension clause.

proof.text: Now prove $\dim X_i=2$ by induction, the case $i=0$ being assumed. Let $b:X_{i+1}\to X_i$ have centre $c$. Every closed point $r$ of $X_{i+1}$ has local dimension at most $2$: if $b(r)=c$, use [lem-sfb-regular-point-blowup-geometry]; otherwise $b$ is an isomorphism near $r$ and identifies its local ring with one on $X_i$. Step 8 bounds the local dimension at every point by that at a closed specialization, and identifies the supremum with scheme dimension, so $\dim X_{i+1}\leq2$. For the reverse inequality, the proper map $b$ has closed image by [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Its image contains $X_i\setminus\{c\}$, which is dense because $X_i$ is integral and has dimension $2$. Thus $b$ is surjective. Choose a point over $c$ and a closed specialization $r$ of it by step 8. Continuity and closedness of $c$ keep $r$ over $c$. The geometry node gives $\dim\mathcal O_{X_{i+1},r}=2$, whence $\dim X_{i+1}\geq2$.

source.place: Tag 0AGR and the closed-point dimension assertion of the global geometry node; dimension preservation in the tower of Tag 0C5H.

proof.text: Each $b_i$ is proper by step 7, so [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition] makes $p$ proper (for length zero, the identity is proper directly from [def-weil-proper-morphism]). Since all centres lie over $T$, composing their isomorphisms off their centres identifies $p^{-1}(V)$ with $V$, and hence $p^{-1}(U)$ with $U$. Define $g=F_Z\circ h$. It is an $S$-morphism, since $qh=p$ and $F_Z$ is over $S$. On $p^{-1}(U)$ the map $h$ lands in $q^{-1}(V)$, and step 5 gives $g=F\circ q\circ h=F\circ p=f\circ p$. Steps 7 and 9 give every asserted property of the intermediate schemes. If $U=X$, choose the length-zero tower and $g=f$; more generally the construction also permits length zero whenever the map already extends.

source.place: Tag 0C5H, proof, final composition; the properness and original-domain compatibility clauses expanded.
